description.narrative: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is the expansion of access to finance for SMEs, including WSMEs and Agri SMEs in Togo. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates a potential to promote greater competitiveness in the SME finance market by demonstrating the commercial viability of lending to SMEs, including WSMEs and Agri SMEs. Assessment of Project Outcome: (i) Stakeholder Effects: Increased Access to Finance for SMEs, including WSMEs and agri SMEs. Due to the low level of financial development, firms in the target country face considerable credit constraints. The proposed intervention by the Project targets a primary binding constraint to get access to finance for SMEs. Assessment of Market Outcomes: (i) Competitiveness: The Project is expected to support the scaling up of an alternative financing product such as leasing that is well suited to meet the needs and risk profiles of SMEs in Togo, thereby increasing the competitive pressures in SME financing; (ii) Resilience: The Project is part of an integral approach to strengthen the resilience of the agricultural supply and value-chain in the African region. Through this Project, IFC intends to contribute to make financing more resilient to financial, economic and climate shocks for Agri SMEs. At least 25 percent of the loan proceeds is expected to be on-lent to Agri SMEs.

The project consist of an unsecured senior loan of up to US$30 million equivalent in Euro, with a maturity of up to 5 years, including a grace period of 12 months, of which IFC's Own Account (O/A) is US$15 million equivalent and the remaining US$15 million equivalent is to be mobilized from other lenders to Africa Lease Togo S.A. (ALT or the Borrower), a new IFC client and largest leasing company in Togo.
